provenance: A native compatibility implementation requiring an installed copy of Pinball Dreams: the package holds only its own code, and the game's tables, pictures and music come from your GOG release each time it runs.

latest.note: On Linux the game is now found where GOG's installer put it, also in a folder of your choice, or where Heroic, Lutris, Minigalaxy, Bottles or Wine put it, and its files are copied as they should be.

brings.title: Starts with a double click
brings.text: No emulator, no DOSBox configuration, nothing to install. On the first start it finds your GOG release by itself, on Linux also one installed with Heroic, Lutris, Bottles or Wine, and copies the game's files.

brings.title: A setup screen before the game
brings.text: In the look of a DOS setup program: start any of the eight tables straight away or go through the game's own menu, and set the options the game hides behind F10.

brings.title: Game controllers
brings.text: Flippers, plunger and nudge on any controller SDL knows (XInput on Windows), each button assignable on the setup screen.

brings.title: Less waiting, if you like
brings.text: Quality of life fixes, each switchable: skip the table animations, shorter silent pauses between balls and at the bonus count. Switched off, the game waits as the original did.

brings.title: The tables as they were
brings.text: The table engine is independently reimplemented in readable C. Its state and behaviour are compared with the original running in an emulated PC, through whole games.

brings.title: Sound and screen
brings.text: Volume, bass, treble and a headphone mode; full screen with Alt+Enter (Cmd+Enter on a Mac).

brings.title: Your things stay yours
brings.text: Settings, saves and high scores live in your user folder: a new version replaces the program's folder and keeps them. It looks for new versions only if you say yes, fetches one small file and sends nothing.
